question.text: This country was the first to mobilize forces to support Serbia, although it withdrew from the war after a 1917 revolution deposed its king Nicholas II.
question.clue: Prince Potemkin had a close relationship with its Catherine the Great.

swap.leadin: This man arrested the "Gang of Eight" which led a coup in August 1991 to remove him from power.
swap.text: Name this Soviet president who was the eighth and final leader of the USSR before its downfall.
swap.clue: Another of his early moves was replacing long-time foreign minister Andrei Gromyko with Eduard Shevardnadze.

question.leadin: In 1978, Georgi Markov died after a ricin-filled pellet was injected into his thigh, probably by an umbrella gun.
question.text: The pellet was allegedly designed by this security agency, led at the time by Yuri Andropov.
question.clue: The GRU was the military counterpart to this organization, which saw many of its agents compromised during the Red Scare.

swap.text: This city located on the Baltic Sea is home to the statue of the Bronze Horseman. It was the capital of the Russian Empire for over two centuries.
swap.clue: The capital of this nation was moved to this city in 1712, and largely remained there until 1918.

question.leadin: The nurse Darya Mikhailova ("mih-HAIL-oh-vuh") took care of Russian soldiers from this war wounded at the Battle of Alma.
question.text: Name this 1853-1856 war, during which Sevastopol ("seh-VAST-oh-pull") was besieged for eleven months. A group of 38 nurses worked at the Scutari Barracks during this war.
question.clue: French forces then trapped the Black Sea fleet during the Siege of Sevastopol.

swap.leadin: This event began when the offices of Rabochi Put were forced to close.
swap.text: Name this event which ended when the Aurora fired a blank shot to signal the capture of the Winter Palace. John Reed chronicled this event in his eyewitness account, Ten Days that Shook the World.
swap.answerHtml: October Revolution [or Bolshevik Revolution; prompt on November Revolution; prompt on Russian Revolution; do NOT accept or prompt on “February Revolution”]
swap.clue: Alexander Kerensky's cadets in Petrograd failed to hold the Winter Palace near the beginning of this event.

question.text: Novgorodian pirates known as Ushkuyniks plied this long Russian river, attacking cities on it such as Kazan and Astrakhan. This river was the main conduit of trade between the Rus and Sassanid Persia.
question.clue: Flowing through Nizhniy Novgorod and Samara, this river's canal to the Don provides the most direct connection between the Sea of Azov (AH-soff) and the world's largest lake.

swap.leadin: He was a sworn brother of the Khan of the Golden Horde, to whom he paid tribute.
swap.text: Name this Grand Prince of Vladimir and Novgorod, a Russian national hero who fought the Teutonic Knights.
swap.clue: This man served as an intermediary between the various Russian rulers and the Mongols under Sartaq Khan of the Golden Horde, whose support made it possible for this man to become Grand Prince of Vladimir.

question.leadin: Identify these uppity groups from Russian history.
question.text: A disagreement between Lenin and Martov led the Mensheviks to break from this group at the Second Party Congress, and later withstood Alexander Bogdanov's recallist movement.
question.clue: This political party, which seized power in the October Revolution, was misleadingly named "the larger party" and was eventually renamed at the 19th Party Congress.

swap.leadin: Identify the following about Russia's Sheremetev ("share-yeh-MYEH-tyef") family.
swap.text: The "improper" clothes worn by Yelena Sheremeteva, the daughter-in-law of this Russian tsar, may have prompted this man to murder his son and heir to the throne in 1581.
swap.answerHtml: Ivan IV [or Ivan the Terrible; or Ivan Grozny; or Ivan the Fearsome; or Ivan the Formidable; or Ioannes Severus; prompt on Ivan]
swap.clue: His person army of men on black horses was called the oprichniki.

question.leadin: Name these places in where news has occurred over the past few years.
question.text: Terrorists affiliated with Chechnyan guerilla leader Shamil Basayev were responsible for the 331 deaths at a school in this North Ossetian city in 2004.

swap.leadin: This ruler murdered his own son, the heir apparent, leading to the incompetent Fyodor the Bellringer coming to power.
swap.text: Name this second-to-last member of the Rurik Dynasty and first Tsar of All the Russias.
swap.answerHtml: Ivan the Terrible [or Ivan IV Vasilyevich; or Ivan Grozny; prompt on Ivan]
swap.clue: This man's suspicion that the Archbishop Pimen was a traitor led to the massacre of Novgorod by his secret police, the Oprichniki.

question.text: This son of Basil III prosecuted the Livonian War and suppressed Novgorod. Ruling from 1547 to 1584, this Rurikid was notable for maintaining the oprichina, a secret police force, and being an all-around mean dude.
question.answerHtml: Ivan IV or Ivan the Terrible [prompt on partial answer]
question.answer: Ivan IV or Ivan the Terrible
question.clue: The Time of Troubles has its roots in the death of this infamous Russia ruler who according to legend blinded the architect of St. Basil's Cathedral.

swap.leadin: In principle, any resident of this city could ring a bell to summon its entire population to either its "Trade" or "Sophia" sides.
swap.text: Name this mercantile city-state that housed the easternmost kontor of the Hanseatic League. This city's conquest by Muscovy after the 1471 Battle of Shelon led to the abolition of its veche ("VETCH-yeh") assembly.
swap.answerHtml: Veliky Novgorod [or Novgorod Republic or Lord Novgorod the Great; reject “Nizhny Novgorod”]
swap.clue: This city's St. Sophia Cathedral is home to the bones of Yaroslav the Wise.

question.leadin: This city's Archbishop Gennadius was responsible for a long held belief that the Heresy of the Judaizers was solely an attempt to introduce Judaism to this city and its country.
question.text: Name this city, which names a republic which allied with Vladimir-Suzdal to defeat the Livonian Order at the Battle of the Ice.
question.clue: This Russian city on the Volkhov River where the Rurikid dynasty ruled until this city's assimilation into the Grand Duchy of Moscow by Ivan III in 1478.

swap.leadin: Because this region lacked its own heraldic shield, English writers punning on its Celtic-inspired name invented a symbol with three yellow grails on a blue background.
swap.text: Name this region of Spain whose city of Santiago de Compostela was often visited as the endpoint of the Way of Saint James, an important pilgrimage of the medieval era.
swap.clue: This region was seized in 1199 by the prince Roman the Great, founding a state that flourished under his son Daniel.

question.leadin: This namesake of a class of icebreaker ships is attested in the charter of Kostroma, which was partially given to his son-in-law Bogdan in tribute to this man's deeds.
question.text: Name this legendary figure, who is said to have led a Polish army looking for the Hypatian Monastery into death in the deep woods instead.

swap.text: The leader of the pro-German government, Pavlo Skoropadskyi, revived the use of this title while leading Ukraine in 1918. This title was traditionally used by leaders of a sich until abolished by Catherine the Great.
swap.clue: Holders of this title, who carried a gem-encrusted mace called a bulawa ("boo-WAH-va"), were elected by the Sich ("seetch") Rada.

question.leadin: This man received a prophecy that his horse would cause his death, which was vindicated years later when a snake emerged from the horse's corpse and fatally bit this man.
question.text: Name this ruler who succeeded his kinsman Rurik and was in turn succeeded by Rurik's son Igor.
question.answerHtml: Oleg of Novgorod [or Oleg the Wise; or Oleg the Seer; or Oleg the Prophet]
question.clue: This man, who killed Askold and Dir to acquire territory, reportedly turned his fleet of longships into horse-drawn tanks and forced Leo VI the Wise to sign a treaty with him in his attack on Constantinople.

swap.text: Things didn't actually stop being troublesome for Russia after the Time of Troubles, as the incompetence of Mstislav the Bold during this 1223 battle led Jebe and Subotai to rampage around the Volga as part of the first major Mongol incursions into Europe. Like every other Russian battle, its named after a body of water.
